gaps.sentence: The house ___ windows were broken has now been sold.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose windows' — the windows belong to the house.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which' and needs no preposition; 'the hotel which we stayed' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: This is the house in ___ I was born.
gaps.explanation: 'In which' is the formal pattern; 'in where' does not exist and 'in that' is impossible in relative clauses.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: The woman ___ won the prize gave a short speech.
gaps.explanation: The gap is the subject pronoun for a person, so 'who' is needed; 'whose' would show possession.

gaps.sentence: There is nothing ___ I would change about the design.
gaps.explanation: After 'nothing', use 'that' (or omit the pronoun); 'which' and 'what' do not fit.
